title: airgap-gpu-image-promotion-and-hsm-signing-pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This page documents the recommended CI/CD and promotion pipeline for GPU runtime images and Terraform artifacts intended for air-gapped / on-prem Redwood Private deployments. The design balances secure provenance (HSM-backed signing and offline attestation), reproducible image promotions, and fast rollback semantics while remaining operable in environments with limited or no outbound network access.

Scope:
- Build and sign GPU node images, container runtimes, and inference runtime bundles.
- Produce Terraform module release artifacts and a promotion flow to on-prem registries/artifact stores.
- Provide an offline verification and attestation process for customer-side import.
- Define rollback and patching runbooks for emergency CVE or kernel regressions.

Intended audience:
- Infra/Platform engineers responsible for Redwood Private on-prem packaging.
- SRE and Security engineers who review supply-chain and signing controls.
- Customer deployment engineers who operate air-gapped cluster ingestion.

Key goals and constraints:
- Cryptographic signing of images and Terraform state/artifacts using HSM (cloud HSM for hosted builds, portable HSM/Nitro enclave for partner builds).
- Minimal trust bootstrap: customers verify signatures and a concise provenance bundle prior to activation.
- Offline-friendly artifact export formats (OCI image tarballs, signed sbom + provenance file, terraform module bundles).
- Fast rollback within a 30-minute window for node image revert with no remote registry access.

High-level architecture (text diagram):

Buildkite/CI --> Build Agents (GPU-enabled) --> Image Signing Service (HSM) --> Artifact Staging (S3/GCS) --> Promotion Orchestrator --> Airgap Export Package

Components and responsibilities:
- CI (Buildkite): orchestrates reproducible builds, runs unit/e2e tests, and produces SBOMs. Uses ephemeral GPU runners with cached dependencies.
- Image Builder: Packer / Kaniko / buildx pipelines that output OCI image manifests and tarballs.
- Signer Service: centralized signing service with HSM (AWS CloudHSM or YubiHSM in SOC2 ops room). Creates detached signatures and a signed provenance JSON (build id, git commit, artifact hashes, sbom hash, signing key id).
- Promotion Orchestrator: a lightweight operator (go) that gamely moves artifacts from staging to the on-prem bundle builder, records promotions in the release ledger (signed), and triggers export packaging.
- Export Package: zip/tar containing images (OCI tarballs), signed provenance.json, sbom.json, terraform-module.tar.gz, and an import-manifest.md with verification steps.

Prerequisites and security controls:
- Attestation keys rotate quarterly via KMS with automated key rotation playbook.
- CI runners must be ephemeral and attested (node attestation) before build job runs.
- All build outputs have SBOM (CycloneDX) and are linked to a reproducible build-id.
- Terraform modules and tfstate schemas are hashed and signed along with images.

CI/CD flow (detailed):
1) Trigger: PR merge to release branch (release/*) or manual release ticket.
2) Build stage (Buildkite):
   - Checkout pinned commit.
   - Run container/image builds with deterministic build args (BUILD_DATE, SOURCE_COMMIT).
   - Produce SBOM and layer hashes (cyclonedx + har).
   - Run unit tests and a small inference smoke test on a canary dataset (sec 60 sec limit).
3) Attestation & Signing:
   - Upload artifacts to a secure staging bucket (private).
   - Invoke Signer Service: request HSM-signed detached signatures and produce provenance.json (signed with a CI release key identifier).
   - Signer returns signature, signing_key_id, and timestamp.
4) Promotion Orchestrator:
   - Default policy: after successful sign and smoke test, mark artifact as candidate.
   - Human approval gate for air-gapped export (2 approvers: Security + Platform).
   - On approval, orchestrator builds Export Package and writes an entry to the release ledger (signed ledger record).
5) Export Packaging:
   - Create OCI tarball with images and include provenance.json + sbom.json + terraform bundle.
   - Run checksum (sha256) for package and sign final package manifest.
6) Delivery:
   - For customer self-pull: provide signed package and instructions for offline import.
   - For partner-managed import: deliver via encrypted removable media and provide HSM public key for verification.

On-prem import and verification (customer steps):
1) Verify package signature using provided public key (commands):
   - sha256sum package.tar.gz && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature package.sig package.tar.gz
2) Unpack and verify image manifests against provenance.json.
3) Load OCI tarballs into private registry (registry restore commands provided).
4) Apply Terraform module bundle to control plane in a dry-run (terraform plan) and verify provider plugin hashes.
5) Run importer verifier script (sh importer-verify.sh) which validates SBOM/ signatures and performs sample inference test on a staging GPU node.

Rollback and emergency patching:
- Rollback windows: we target 30-minute rollback to previously signed image. Achieved by: keeping last three signed images in local cache + enabling offline revert script on node provisioning host.
- Emergency CVE process:
  1. Create hotfix branch and trigger emergency build (fast-path CI).
  2. Sign and package with expedited approvals (automated security scan + single approver from Security on-call).
  3. Distribute hotfix bundle using the same airgap process and follow immediate apply with accelerated cluster drain window.
- Rollback runbook steps (abridged):
  1. Identify bad promotion id in release ledger.
  2. On the provisioning host, run revert script: ./revert-to-image.sh --promotion-id <id> --nodes <node-group>.
  3. Verify node rejoin and warm KV cache seed (run kv-cache-warmup job).
  4. Monitor errors for 15 minutes; if degradation persists, escalate to SRE on-call.

Testing matrix and CI gates:
- Required gates for promotion: unit tests, deterministic-image-hash-check, SBOM completeness, kernel compatibility check, inference smoke test (latency < 300ms, output sanity pass), security static scan (SCA) pass.
- Optional gates for expedited path: allow skip of non-blocking long-running integration tests with explicit human acknowledgement.

Terraform + IaC considerations:
- Terraform module bundles are versioned with semver and a signed CHANGES.md.
- The Orchestrator embeds a ‘tf-lock.json’ snapshot to ensure providers and plugin binaries match the promoted artifact.
- For customers who cannot run provider plugins from public registries, we include a provider plugin bundle with SHA256 and signature.

Operational runbook snippets (actionable):
- Verify a package: ./tools/verify-package --package ./package.tar.gz --key ./public.pem  # exits non-zero on mismatch
- Load images to local registry: ctr image import images.tar  # followed by registry sync script
- Import terraform bundle: tar -xzf tf-modules.tar.gz && terraform init -plugin-dir=./plugins && terraform plan
- Force revert of nodes: ./scripts/force-node-revert.sh --group infra-gpu-01 --image-id <signed-image-id> --reason "kernel-regression"

SLOs and operational thresholds for private deployments (recommendation):
- Promotion time-to-deliver (signed package ready): <= 2 hours for standard releases, <= 30 minutes for hotfixes.
- Verification time (customer import verification): <= 60 minutes (documented walk-through helps).
- Rollback completion: <= 30 minutes to restore previously known-good image on affected node group.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: infra-release-team (Platform) — paged via #infra-release and on-call rotation.
- Security owner: sec-supply-chain — must approve airgap promotions.
- Escalation path: on-call infra -> infra-release lead -> sec lead -> CTO if cross-customer outage.

Open decisions and follow-ups:
- Decide whether to embed signed kernel modules in the image or provide separately as a module bundle for customers who require FIPS/HSM validation.
- Evaluate using in-toto for richer provenance (action: prototype Q4 2025).
- Pilot local YubiHSM workflow with two customers in EU (action: schedule workshops).

References and related pages:
- Preflight acceptance checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/preflight-private-deploy-acceptance-checklist
- Signed runtime verifier guidelines: /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/signed-gpu-runtime-bundle-and-verifier-guidelines.json
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/preflight-gpu-deployment-validation-and-rollback-playbook.json

Appendix: sample commands and policy table

Table: signing policy (summary)
- signing_key_rotation: quarterly
- hsm_mandatory: for release and hotfix channels
- storage_encryption: AES-256 at rest for staging buckets
- approvers_required: 2 (security + platform)

Sample verification snippet:
- openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature package.sig package.tar.gz
- jq -r .build_id provenance.json | xargs -I{} ./tools/attest-check --id {}
